page: Microsoft Azure D64d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. It runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, offering 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor package provides 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and support for vector instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI. The instance includes 256.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, alongside 2,577 GB of bundled local SSD storage. It operates without dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent computational throughput with strong uncached memory and vector capabilities. The system achieved a PassMark CPU score of 46,461.57 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,287.0, both placing within average ranges. However, it achieved top-quartile results in extended vector instruction testing with a PassMark score of 53,854.89, as well as PassMark database operations scoring 22,475.92. Memory bandwidth is notably high for large blocks, registering 208.41 GB/sec for uncached reads and 93.84 GB/sec for writes, both belonging to the top 25% tier. Conversely, text generation tasks in LLM inference benchmarks performed weakly, reflecting typical latency constraints for large language model decoding on non-accelerated CPU architectures.

The D64d_v4 demonstrates strong resource density for enterprise workloads requiring ample memory bandwidth paired with high-capacity local temporary storage. The integration of 2,577 GB of local SSD provides fast scratch space and caching capabilities without external disk latency overhead. This configuration is particularly suited for high-throughput relational databases, in-memory caching solutions, enterprise application servers, data transformation pipelines, and parallel compilation tasks.
